title: Finite quotient fraction fields above a principal prime
statement: Let R be a Noetherian domain, S a domain over R, and K and L their fraction fields, with compatible maps R -> K -> L and R -> S -> L. Assume L is finite-dimensional over K. Let Q be a prime of S whose contraction is the principal ideal xR. Then the canonical extension FractionRing(S/Q) over FractionRing(R/(Q contraction)) is finite-dimensional. Neither integrality nor normality nor an N-2 hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 032P, the application of Tag 031F and identification of prime residue fields (steps 4-5 of the parent); x=0 uses finite-dimensional domains over a field

proof.text: If x=0, the contraction p is zero. For any s in Q, finite-dimensionality of L/K gives algebraicity of its image in L over K. IsFractionRing.isAlgebraic_iff clears denominators to give algebraicity over R, and isAlgebraic_algebraMap_iff pulls this back along the injection S -> L. If s were nonzero, Ideal.comap_ne_bot_of_algebraic_mem would contradict p=0. Thus Q=0. Use quotientBot to equip K and L with the quotient algebra structures and identify their fraction rings. IsFractionRing.algEquiv_commutes proves compatibility of the two field equivalences; Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv transports the given finiteness.

If x is nonzero, x is a nonunit because p=xR is prime. Mathlib Ideal.height_span_singleton_eq_one_of_mem_nonZeroDivisors gives p.height=1, using that a nonzero element of a domain is a non-zero-divisor. IsLocalization.AtPrime.ringKrullDim_eq_height identifies this with the dimension of Rp=R_p. The localization is Noetherian.

Set Sp=S_Q and let phi:Rp -> Sp be Localization.localRingHom. Equip Rp -> K and Sp -> L with localizationAlgebraOfSubmonoidLe and use isFractionRing_of_isDomain_of_isLocalization to retain the fraction fields. IsLocalization.ringHom_ext, the original scalar towers, and localRingHom_to_map show algebraMap K L composed with Rp -> K equals Sp -> L composed with phi. This implies phi is injective. Its maximal ideal contracts to the base maximal ideal by IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal_comap. Apply Ideal.dim_one_residue_fields_finite to the maximal prime of Sp, obtaining finiteness of the residue extension.

The maps from R to Rp and S to Sp are surjective on stalks. RingHom.SurjectiveOnStalks.residueFieldMap_bijective supplies ring equivalences from p.ResidueField to the residue field of the maximal prime of Rp, and from Q.ResidueField to the analogous field for Sp. Give the latter fields their quotient algebras using these maps. On quotient generators, three applications of Ideal.ResidueField.map_algebraMap and localRingHom_to_map verify the scalar tower between the two quotient rings and these fields. IsFractionRing.of_algEquiv makes them fraction fields of R/p and S/Q. Finally, IsFractionRing.algEquiv_commutes and Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv transport finite-dimensionality to the canonical FractionRing extension, via the proved private helper finite_fraction_transport.

theorem principal_prime_quotient_fraction_finite
    (R : Type uR) (S : Type uS) (K : Type uK) (L : Type uL)
    [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [CommRing S] [IsDomain S] [Algebra R S]
    [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
    [Algebra S L] [IsFractionRing S L] [Algebra K L] [Algebra R L]
    [IsScalarTower R K L] [IsScalarTower R S L] [FiniteDimensional K L]
    (x : R) (Q : Ideal S) [Q.IsPrime]
    (hcontract : Q.comap (algebraMap R S) = Ideal.span ({x} : Set R)) :
    letI : FaithfulSMul (R ⧸ Q.comap (algebraMap R S)) (S ⧸ Q) :=
      (faithfulSMul_iff_algebraMap_injective _ _).mpr Ideal.algebraMap_quotient_injective
    FiniteDimensional (FractionRing (R ⧸ Q.comap (algebraMap R S)))
      (FractionRing (S ⧸ Q))
